# Paw & Prosper -- Full Content Reference

## About

Paw & Prosper is a digital marketing consultancy specializing in SEO and AI visibility systems for animal wellness businesses. Founded by Samantha Quinones, the company works exclusively with veterinarians, pet brands, animal shelters, animal rescues, groomers, trainers, boarding/daycare facilities, and other pet service businesses.

The company's core belief: the animal wellness industry deserves specialized marketing expertise, not generic agency work. Pet parents now search across both traditional search engines and AI assistants, and businesses that aren't visible in both places are missing clients.

Samantha Quinones is a digital marketer with over 12 years of experience in SEO and AI search optimization. She created Paw & Prosper after seeing how many high-quality animal wellness businesses were invisible online -- not because their work wasn't excellent, but because they lacked the right visibility strategy. Outside of work, she's a dog mom to Itachi, a Lab-Collie mix, and volunteers at her local animal shelter.

Paw & Prosper offers nonprofit pricing to animal shelters, rescues, and animal welfare nonprofits. Reduced monthly rates, free workshops on Google and AI visibility, bonus audits, and case study collaborations.

Contact: samantha@pawandprosper.com

## Core Services

### Local SEO Optimization
Helps pet businesses rank higher in Google and local search results. Includes keyword strategy, Google Business Profile optimization, local citation building, on-page SEO, and technical SEO.

### AI Visibility & LLM Optimization
Optimizes business content so AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) accurately represent and recommend the business. Includes structured data implementation, content formatting for AI ingestion, and AI citation monitoring.

### Content Strategy & Authority Building
Builds topical authority through SEO-optimized blog content, service page optimization, and educational resources that rank in search and get cited by AI tools.

## Who We Serve

- Independent Veterinary Clinics: Independent and specialty vet practices competing with corporate chains (Banfield, VCA, BluePearl, National Veterinary Associates). Corporate groups have national ad budgets and dedicated SEO teams. Paw & Prosper helps independent practices compete on strategy, community trust, and organic visibility. Focus on local search, emergency and specialty search terms, and AI recommendations for pet health questions.
- Animal Shelters: Public and nonprofit shelters seeking more adoptions, donations, and volunteers through improved search presence and community visibility. Both municipal animal control facilities and 501(c)(3) nonprofits. Includes Google Business Profile optimization, review strategy, and local search visibility.
- Animal Rescues: Foster-based and breed-specific rescue organizations. Rescues face unique SEO challenges: no physical storefront, geographically dispersed foster networks, and the need to reach adopters, fosters, and donors simultaneously. Breed-specific rescues have strong long-tail keyword advantages. Paw & Prosper builds visibility strategies designed for how rescues actually operate.
- Pet Brands: E-commerce and DTC pet product companies (food, supplements, accessories, gear) wanting organic traffic and AI-powered product discovery. Focus on product page SEO, category optimization, brand authority, and reducing paid ad dependence.
- Pet Services: Groomers, trainers, boarding/daycare facilities, holistic pet wellness practitioners, and other local pet service businesses. Focus on local search, Google Maps visibility, and AI assistant recommendations.

## Case Studies

### Lone Star Animal Welfare League: 32x Google Visibility Growth in Six Months
LSAWL is a low-cost spay and neuter nonprofit serving Montgomery County, Texas (The Woodlands area). Starting from near-zero online visibility with no paid advertising budget, LSAWL worked with Paw & Prosper on local SEO and AI visibility optimization. Result: 32x growth in Google search visibility in six months, with no paid ad spend. Full case study: https://pawandprosper.com/how-lone-star-animal-welfare-league-grew-google-visibility-32x-in-six-months-no-ad-spend

## Blog Content

### How to Check if AI Recommends Your Pet Business (and What to Fix First)

URL: https://pawandprosper.com/blog/how-to-check-if-ai-recommends-your-pet-business

Three copy-paste tests (AI names you for the best near you, AI describes you correctly, trusted sites list you), a table for reading results, and the fix order for pet businesses: complete the Google Business Profile and primary category, weekly reviews with replies, consistent listings and local mentions, a page per service, answer-first openings.

### What Evertune's Pet Industry Data Says About AI Search
URL: https://pawandprosper.com/blog/what-evertunes-pet-industry-data-says-about-ai-search
Published: October 30, 2026
Author: Samantha Quinones, Founder & SEO Strategist at Paw & Prosper
Summary: A look at Evertune's pet food and pet supplies AI visibility reports (June to August 2026), with credit to Evertune for the data. In pet food, Purina reached an organic visibility score of 100 by August; in pet supplies no brand scored above 40, leaving room for smaller brands. Several big pet brands tested ads inside ChatGPT and turned them off within a month or two. For local services like vet clinics, AI ads are close to nonexistent, so organic visibility is the opportunity, and AI tools cite reviews, lists, directories and partner sites more than a business's own website. Includes what vets, pet brands and pet service businesses should do, plus an FAQ.

### What AI Looks At Before It Recommends a Vet
URL: https://pawandprosper.com/blog/what-ai-looks-at-before-it-recommends-a-vet
Published: October 25, 2026
Author: Samantha Quinones, Founder & SEO Strategist at Paw & Prosper
Summary: Results of live tests asking ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Mode for the best vet in Summit County, Colorado, in September and October 2026. The recommendations changed between months and between tools. Three patterns shaped what AI said: local recognition (awards and news coverage), plain service wording on practice websites, and practical details like hours. Documents AI errors (a false "only clinic" claim, a clinic from Summit County, Ohio, a permanently closed practice) and gives independent practices a checklist plus an FAQ.

## The Problem We Solve

Pet parents now use multiple search surfaces to find pet services and products:
1. Traditional Google Search ("vet near me", "best grain-free dog food")
2. Google Maps and local pack results
3. AI assistants ("which vet in my area is best for anxious dogs?", "recommend a natural supplement for senior cats")

Most animal wellness businesses are optimized for none of these, or at best one. Paw & Prosper builds visibility systems that work across all three.

## Our Process

1. Free Visibility Audit: Analyze the business's current presence across Google, AI assistants, and local directories.
2. Custom Insights Report: Detailed breakdown of visibility gaps, quick wins, and long-term opportunities.
3. Strategy Call: Walk through findings and discuss a tailored plan.
4. Ongoing Optimization: Monthly work that compounds visibility over time.

## Key Differentiators

- Exclusively serves the animal wellness industry
- Combines traditional SEO with AI visibility optimization (most agencies do one or the other)
- Independent business working with independent businesses -- no national agency account handoffs
- Nonprofit pricing for animal shelters, rescues, and animal welfare organizations
- Founder has 12+ years of digital marketing experience and personally volunteers in animal welfare
- Focuses on long-term organic visibility, not just paid traffic

## Free Resource: The Unmissable Checklist

URL: https://pawandprosper.com/ai-visibility-checklist

A free, 20-point self-audit that shows whether ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google can find, understand and trust a pet business (vets, groomers, boarding and daycare, trainers, pet brands, rescues). Each check takes under 2 minutes and is worth 5 points. Bands: 0 to 49 Invisible, 50 to 74 Findable, 75 to 100 Unmissable. It is a simplified version of the Unmissable Index, the four-pillar framework Samantha Quinones uses in paid audits. The checks are signals search engines and AI tools are known to use, not a guaranteed formula.

**Pillar 1: Technical Foundation (20 points).** Can Google and AI tools reach and read your website?

1. Your site loads fast on a phone: Most people find you on their phone. Slow pages lose them before they ever see your services.
2. Google has your important pages: If Google hasn't indexed a page, neither Google Search nor its AI answers can show it.
3. Your site tells machines who you are: Schema markup is a hidden label on your site that spells out your business type, address, phone and hours for search engines.
4. AI tools are allowed to read your site: A file called robots.txt can quietly block the crawlers AI search tools use to read your site.

**Pillar 2: Authority Engine (20 points).** Does your website prove you know your stuff?

5. Every main service has its own page: One “Services” page with a bullet list gives Google and AI nothing specific to match or quote.
6. You have helpful guides, not just sales pages: AI tools recommend the businesses that explain things well. Guides show you're the expert.
7. Something new or updated in the last 90 days: Fresh, accurate pages tell people and machines you're open, active and current.
8. Your pages link to each other and to booking: Links between your pages help Google find everything and help visitors take the next step.

**Pillar 3: AI & Search Optimization (20 points).** When someone asks AI, are you the answer?

9. AI names you when asked for the best near you: The core test: when a customer asks an AI assistant for a recommendation, are you in the answer?
10. AI describes you correctly: Being mentioned isn't enough. AI has to get your services, location and reputation right.
11. Your first two sentences say what you do and where: AI tools quote short passages. Pages that answer up front are the easiest to quote.
12. You have a real FAQ: People now type full questions into search and AI. A good FAQ answers them in your words.

**Pillar 4: Local & Trust Signals (40 points).** Do Google and AI trust you enough to recommend you?

13. Your Google Business Profile is claimed and complete: Your Google profile feeds Google Maps and Google's AI answers, and other AI tools read it too.
14. Your Google Business Profile category is the right one: Your primary category tells Google which searches you're relevant for, and relevance is one of the three things Google says local results depend on.
15. Your review count keeps up with the top 3: Google says review count and rating factor into local ranking, and AI tools summarize your reviews for shoppers.
16. A strong rating, with a review in the last 30 days: Shoppers trust recent reviews, and so do the tools that summarize them.
17. You reply to every review: Replies show you're paying attention, and they add fresh, specific detail about your services.
18. New photos and a post in the last 30 days: An active profile looks open and trustworthy. A stale one looks closed.
19. You're in the top 3 on the map for your main search: The top 3 map results are what people see first on their phone, before they scroll or ask anything else.
20. Trusted sites list you, with matching details: Before recommending you, AI tools cross-check what other sites say about you.
